email.body1:
Ryan, saw Anaqua acquire Patrix, adding 400 customers and deepening your law-firm and European reach after RightHub.

Absorbing that many new accounts usually means more firms and corporates in play than the team can personally cover, especially right after a deal closes, and that is where revenue leaks. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new hires: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Anaqua off your acquisition and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. As CRO, worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Ryan, quick follow-up for Anaqua.

With 400 Patrix customers folding in, the cross-sell and net-new surface is large, but most teams do not actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the number. The gap shows up late, and then the quarter is a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Anaqua needs to hit target this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Ryan, last bit of proof for Anaqua.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Anaqua's reply rate likely compares to other enterprise-software companies. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Ryan, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Integrating a 400-customer acquisition is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I will tailor it to Anaqua either way.
